subject: Asking question about missing observations in latent growth model

messages.author: d8517e92c7758dc2
messages.subject: Asking question about missing observations in latent growth model
parts:
Hi Professors, 

I would like to ask one question about the missing observations when I fit a latent growth model. 

I have repeated measured one variable denoted as x variable at 6 time points, but the observations of x variable at the last time point was largely less than the observations in the previous time points, for example, there were 450, 420, 320, 280, 260, and 40 observations for x variable from time1 to time6, respectively. In this situatioin when I fit a latent growth model for x variable, shall I drop the observations of x in the last time piont (only use the measurements in the first five time points) to let the model more convergable? 

By the way, I have several x variables, and I would like to establish the latent growth model for each of these x variables. The results were, for some of the x variables, I could get convergable model by using either 5 time points measurements or 6 time points measurements, but for some other x variables, the model is only convergable for the 5 time points measurements. Moreover, growth model with 5 time points seems to have better model fit measurements than the model using 6 time pionts. So coming back to my question above, shall I use 5 time-points to fit the growth model for all x variables, or choose best specific model for each x variable? 

Regards 

Xueying

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Asking question about missing observations in latent growth model
parts:
Xueying,

Even aside from convergence, I'd be skeptical that the drastic drop in sample to time 6 can be considered missing at random. Unless you have some conceptually and methodologically sound way to accommodate non-random missingness here, I recommend omitting it from all analyses.

Pat
